{{Top}}
[[File:Sithcode.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Darth Krayt]] recites the Code on Korriban.]]
{{Quote|I am not a man of words. But I respect the power of words, for that is what transformed me. The words of the Sith Code. Others had heard them, contemplated them, and so on. But I understood them, and they changed me. For what was I before I heard those words? Nothing.|[[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]|<ref name="JVSEGF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
The '''Code of the Sith''', known as '''Qotsisajak''' in [[Sith (language)|Sith]], was the mantra that reinforced the core beliefs of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]]. It was considered the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] counterpart to the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]], and was first authored on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] in [[6900 BBY]] by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Jedi heretic]] [[Sorzus Syn]]. The code remained remarkably unchanged through the millennia, as the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] still taught the words of Sorzus Syn when he began rebuilding the Sith Order around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]].

==The Sith Code==
{{Quote|Brazen and shameless, and at their own mortal peril, they had waged etheric war, anticipating that their own midi-chlorians, the Force's proxy army, might marshal to boil their blood or stop the beating of their hearts. Risen out of themselves, discorporate and as a single entity, they had brought the power of their will to bear, asserting their sovereignty over the Force.|Darth Plagueis|<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
The Sith Code, as written by [[Sorzus Syn]]<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> and taught by [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]:<ref name="DBRT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>
<poem>
''Peace is a lie, there is only passion.
''Through passion, I gain strength.
''Through strength, I gain power.
''Through power, I gain victory.
''Through victory, my chains are broken.
''The Force shall free me.
</poem>

There also existed a version of the code in [[Sith (language)|Sith]], known as ''Qotsisajak''&mdash;literally "Way of the Sith doctrine":<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail2">{{EmailCite|email=Wookieepedia:Email/Ben Grossblatt (2013)|creator=[[Ben Grossblatt]]|date=2012-07-25}}</ref>
<poem>
''Nwûl tash.
''Dzwol shâsotkun.
''Shâsotjontû châtsatul nu tyûk.
''Tyûkjontû châtsatul nu midwan.
''Midwanjontû châtsatul nu asha.
''Ashajontû kotswinot itsu nuyak.
''Wonoksh Qyâsik nun.
</poem>

==History==
{{Quote|A single, unifying code can be derived from the Sith philosophy. The Jedi have a code, and we exiles know it well. But we also know it is full of inadequacies and half-truths.|Sorzus Syn|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[File:Code_of_the_Sith.png|thumb|left|250px|The Code of the Sith, as penned by Sorzus Syn herself around 6900 BBY]]
According to the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Qordis]], founder and master of the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], the Code of the Sith served as the backbone of the Order since [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Exiles]] enslaved the [[Color/Legends|red]]-skinned [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith Purebloods]] from the [[Horuset system]].<ref name="JVSEGF" /> Indeed, the first recorded appearance of the Code dates back to the personal journal of Sorzus Syn, one of the fallen Jedi who set foot on Korriban in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[6900 BBY]].<ref name="BOS" />

Syn had been impressed by the lifestyle of the Sith Purebloods, who would take all what they needed, kill the rest, and use everything to its fullest. Inspired by their example of brutal impulsiveness, Syn decided to write a pendant to the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]], a new mantra that was based on passion and the channeling of rage through anger. In her journal, Sorzus Syn claimed that the Jedi beliefs only encouraged acceptance of one's limitations and passivity. The Sith Code was created on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] so as to point to the "failings" of the Jedi Code, and it was meant to become a unifying mantra for the followers of the newly created [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="BOS" />

By [[990 BBY]], the Jedi Order knew of the Sith Code. In ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'', the Human [[Chief Librarian/Legends|Chief Librarian]] [[Restelly Quist/Legends|Restelly Quist]] wrote a chapter on Sith history, including a brief commentary on the Code of the Sith. According to [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] Quist, the tenets of the Sith were self-centered and focused on individual needs and desires, while the Jedi defended the idea of achieving greatness through self-humbling.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

==Analysis of the Sith Code==
{{Quote|The tenets of the Sith are more than just words to be memorized. Learn them, understand them. They will lead you to the true power of the Force; the power of the dark side.|[[Qordis]]|<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref>}}
Some have speculated that the Code of the Sith was created in direct contrast with the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]], to illustrate the fundamental philosophical differences between the orders. This could certainly account for the first line of the Sith Code discounting the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] proclamation of peace, as well as the similar structure of the two Codes, although the Jedi claimed the Code spoke only of the Sith's individual wants and desires.

===''Peace is a lie, there is only passion''===
{{Quote|Conflict forces one to better oneself. It forces change, growth, adaption, evolution… or death.|[[Yuthura Ban]]|<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
According to [[Yuthura Ban]], a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] Sith practitioner who taught at the Korriban Academy, the "peace" of the Jedi, meaning the lack of conflict, was an agent of stagnation. Conflict, however, was seen as the source of progress for both the single beings and the civilizations. She also claimed that the necessity of conflict was a law of the universe and not just a Sith thinking.<ref name="KOTOR" />
Fundamentally, the Code of the Sith expressed their rejection of selflessness and their full embrace of passion and lust. Although some individuals turned to the dark side out of a philosophical ideal or even wished to wield its violent powers for altruistic purposes, all Sith ended up prisoners of their own crave for power. The deeper nature of the Sith Order was a predatory one,<ref name="WIZ">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/BtT1|series=Behind the Threat: The Sith|text=Part 1: Portrayal}}</ref> a trait that Sorzus Syn had admired in the Sith Purebloods.<ref name="BOS" />

===''Through passion, I gain strength.''===
{{Quote|It is our goal to be stronger, to achieve our potential and not rest upon our laurels. We are the seekers, not the shepherds.|Yuthura Ban|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The Sith saw themselves as seekers, challengers of old and stagnant ways, in touch with the laws of nature and the universe. They saw the Jedi as denying their natures and afraid of the truth around them. Yuthura Ban gave examples of the [[Tuk'ata/Legends|tuk'ata]] hunting prey, feeding on weaker creatures. Passions were what kept all creatures&mdash;from the most rudimentary to the most evolved sentient&mdash;alive. Yuthura Ban explained this to the amnesiac [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], ''"To think us creatures beyond the need of simple passions is a delusion."'' They believed that mastery of their passions gave them strength the Jedi lacked.<ref name="KOTOR" />

===''Through strength, I gain power''===
{{Quote|Without strife, the victory has no meaning. Without strife, one does not advance. Without strife, there is only stagnation.|Yuthura Ban|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The Sith is defined by the pursuit of power. To seek power, they draw strength from emotions such as pain, anger, and hate - emotions that the Jedi seek to overcome.<ref name="WIZ" /> Throughout history, many Sith attempted to achieve absolute power by conquering the galaxy, either through brute force or cunning. To the Sith, power is its own reward, as gaining power is necessary to achieve individual freedom and freeing one from limitations.

===''Through power, I gain victory''===
{{Quote|Unless the victory is achieved by demonstrating that your power is superior, it is only an illusion. Temporary at best. We seek more.|Yuthura Ban|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The Sith did not believe that victory by any means was desirable, but believed that unless victory proved your superiority, it was an illusion and temporary. Though there might be different types of victories&mdash;peaceful victory, victory by sacrifice, even a truce&mdash;Sith dogma taught that unless the victory was achieved by demonstrating that one's power was superior, it was not true victory. The stronger a Sith became in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the more power he could achieve, but he always had to fight for that power.<ref name="KOTOR" />

===''Through victory, my chains are broken''===
{{Quote|One who has freed themselves from all restrictions has reached perfection… their potential fulfilled. Perfect strength, perfect power, perfect destiny.|Yuthura Ban|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The true meaning of the line "&hellip;my chains are broken" was a subject of argument among many Sith. According to Yuthura Ban, the chains represented a being's restrictions; not just a Sith but any being in the universe. The restrictions could be those placed upon a being by someone else, or restrictions that one placed upon oneself. The ultimate goal of any Sith was to free himself from such restrictions, but not in the simplistic meaning of just being able to do whatever he wanted. The Sith desired to free themselves in order to reach perfection and fulfill their potential. They wanted perfect strength, perfect power, and perfect destiny, which, in turn, allowed one to do whatever they wanted for the most part. The person who had these abilities was known as the [[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]].<ref name="KOTOR" />

The Sith'ari was supposed to destroy the Sith and then make them stronger than ever. This caused many Sith to treat perfection as a goal to work towards rather than a strict state of being, and in that way they were very like the Jedi.<ref name="KOTOR" /> General historical consensus has considered [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] to be the Sith'ari.<ref name="cswe">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Indeed, Bane destroyed the Sith using the [[thought bomb]] at the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]] in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] and rebuilt it under the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]], which would ultimately lead to Sith domination of the galaxy in the form of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="BOS" />

===''The Force shall free me.''===
{{Quote|The Force is our servant and our master. Our teacher and our companion. A weapon and a tool. Know it and you know the universe. Master it and you master the universe. Strive for perfection and the Force shall reward you.|Yuthura Ban|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The Sith believed that those who strove for perfection through knowledge and mastery of the Force would be rewarded. The Sith also believed that those who followed their code were free of the mundane restrictions of others, that they strove for a greater purpose and thus threw off the restrictions normally placed upon individuals by society and other organizations.<ref name="episode III novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Sith Lords tried to put the Force itself, in all its aspects, to their service.<ref name="DP" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Code of the Sith was created by [[David Gaider]], who wrote the Korriban segment of the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. Initially, Gaider had asked [[Lucasfilm]] whether the Sith had a written creed like the Jedi did. When he was told to write one specifically for the game, Gaider reversed the existing Jedi Code and complemented it with a Sith philosophy partly inspired by [[Wikipedia:Mein Kampf|''Mein Kampf'']], the infamous autobiographical manifesto written by the [[Wikipedia:Nazism|Nazi]] leader [[Wikipedia:Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler]].<ref name="Gaider">{{Tumblr|subdomain=the-gaider-archives|url=post/108932517363/on-knights-of-the-old-republic|name=DGaider Tumblr Archives|text=On Knights of the Old Republic}}</ref>
